quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Product Review] I bought these headphones for my daily train journey, and for that purpose they're excellent: the noise cancelling takes the edge off the engine rumble, and the battery lasted a full week of commuting. Sound quality is where opinions split. Reviewers who listen to classical music praise the clarity, but I found the bass boomy and had to adjust the equalizer before songs sounded balanced. Comfort is another mixed point; after ninety minutes my ears were warm. At this price, I'd recommend them to commuters rather than to anyone who cares mostly about music.
quests.question: What is the reviewer's overall recommendation?
options: They are the ideal choice for people who mostly listen at home.
They are a good choice for commuters but less so for music lovers.
They are too expensive and should not be bought by anyone.
They are best suited to people who listen to classical music.
quests.correctAnswer: They are a good choice for commuters but less so for music lovers.
quests.hint: The last sentence sums up who the reviewer would and would not recommend them to.
quests.explanation: The reviewer praises the headphones for commuting but has reservations about sound and comfort, so recommends them to commuters rather than music lovers.
quests.evidenceLine: I'd recommend them to commuters rather than to anyone who cares mostly about music

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Mangroves and Storms] Mangrove forests grow along tropical coasts, their tangled roots rising out of salty mud. Those roots slow incoming waves, so a belt of mangroves can reduce a wave's force before it reaches the shore. After a severe cyclone struck one coastal region, villages sheltered by mangroves reported far less flooding than neighboring villages without them. Mangroves also trap sediment, which gradually builds up the land, and they provide nurseries for young fish. Despite these benefits, many forests have been cleared for shrimp farms, leaving communities more exposed.
quests.question: What central message does the text about mangroves convey?
options: The protective and ecological value of mangroves
How shrimp farms are built and run in the tropics
The effect of severe cyclones on fish populations
Why the water along tropical coasts is salty
quests.correctAnswer: The protective and ecological value of mangroves
quests.hint: Decide which idea ties together the roots, the storm evidence and the clearing of forests.
quests.explanation: Every sentence deals with what mangroves do for coasts, communities and fish, and what is lost when they are cleared.
quests.evidenceLine: so a belt of mangroves can reduce a wave's force before it reaches the shore

quests.passage: [First Paycheck] When Dario opened the envelope, the number on the slip was smaller than he'd calculated. He was paid at a lower rate.
quests.correctAnswer: He forgot that taxes would be deducted.

quests.explanation: Dario multiplied his hours but forgot that taxes would be taken out first, so the amount he received was lower.
quests.evidenceLine: forgotten that taxes would be taken out first

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Choosing Rental Insurance] Rental companies usually offer two levels of cover. Basic cover costs $12 a day and includes theft protection, but the driver pays the first $1,500 of any damage. Full cover costs $28 a day and reduces that amount to zero. Many credit cards already include some rental insurance, so it is worth checking before you pay for extra cover. For a short trip on quiet country roads, basic cover may be enough; for a week in heavy city traffic, many drivers feel the extra $16 a day is worth the peace of mind.
quests.question: What is the main difference between the two levels of cover?
options: Only full cover includes protection against theft.
Only full cover can be booked on the company's website.
Basic cover lasts for a week longer than full cover.
Under full cover the driver pays nothing toward damage.
quests.correctAnswer: Under full cover the driver pays nothing toward damage.
quests.hint: Compare what the driver has to pay under each level.
quests.explanation: Under basic cover the driver pays the first $1,500 of damage, while full cover reduces that amount to zero.
quests.evidenceLine: Full cover costs $28 a day and reduces that amount to zero

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Reviving the High Street] When the supermarket on the edge of town opened, many shops on Mill Street lost customers and a third of them closed. The council's solution was not to ban the supermarket but to make the high street worth visiting. It cut parking fees to a flat $1 after 4 p.m., allowed cafés to put tables on the pavement, and invited small markets on Saturdays. Within two years, only four units stood empty, down from eleven. Local business owners credit the markets in particular, though some say the change in parking made the biggest difference.
quests.question: How did the council respond to the loss of customers?
options: It made the high street more attractive to visit.
It banned the supermarket on the edge of town.
It closed Mill Street to all cars and buses.
It paid shopkeepers directly for lost sales.
quests.correctAnswer: It made the high street more attractive to visit.
quests.hint: The second sentence contrasts what the council did not do with what it did.
quests.explanation: The council did not ban the supermarket but tried to make the high street worth visiting through lower parking fees, café tables and markets.
quests.evidenceLine: make the high street worth visiting

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Why I Stopped Checking Email Constantly] For years I checked my inbox every few minutes, convinced that fast replies made me a better colleague. Then I tracked my day and found that I spent nearly two hours on email, most of it in small interruptions that broke up my real work. Now I check three times a day, at nine, noon, and four, and I add a line to my signature explaining why. Nobody has complained. A few people have even copied the idea, which was not why I did it, but I admit it feels good.

To advertise a new email program to readers
To report the results of a workplace survey
To explain a change in habit and why it was made

quests.explanation: The writer describes an old habit, the reason for changing it and the results of the new routine.
quests.evidenceLine: Now I check three times a day

quests.passage: [Harbor at Dawn] By half past five, the harbor had begun to stir. Fishing crews moved along the quay in the gray light, hauling crates and calling to one another in short, practiced phrases. Gulls circled above the boats, waiting for scraps. The café at the end of the pier had just switched on its lights, and the smell of fresh coffee drifted over the water. Nobody hurried; the work had a rhythm that came from repetition. Only the tourists, who would not arrive for hours, would later describe the scene as peaceful. For those inside it, it was simply morning.
quests.question: What does "the work had a rhythm that came from repetition" suggest?
options: The workers were bored and feeling very tired.
The workers were singing together as they worked.
The workers moved calmly through familiar tasks.
The workers were new to the job and nervous.
quests.correctAnswer: The workers moved calmly through familiar tasks.
quests.hint: Consider what repeating a task every day does to how a person does it.
quests.explanation: A rhythm built from repetition suggests familiar tasks done smoothly and without rush, which fits "Nobody hurried".
quests.evidenceLine: the work had a rhythm that came from repetition
